Int4 MoE decode on Xe2 spends most of its expert time in the fixed cost of .
At one decode token with top-8 routing each expert sees one row.
On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (GPTQ int4 experts), the 8 active experts of a layer are 13 MB of weights, about 21 us at the B70's bandwidth, but a gate_up call takes ~56 us and a down call ~34 us.
This PR adds , a SYCL GEMV for the int4 layout the grouped GEMM already uses (int8-packed signed 4-bit from , per-group scales in the activation dtype).
routes int4 calls with at most 8 rows to it (); larger calls (prefill, MTP verify, batched decode) keep the grouped GEMM.
Kernel: one work-group per (active expert, block of N).
The work-group finds its expert with a group scan over (no host sync, works under graph capture).
Each sub-group computes 4 output columns for up to 2 rows at a time, lanes split K in chunks of 32 int4 values (16-byte weight loads), fp32 accumulation, per-group scale applied per chunk.
Related: #509 (fixed per-step MoE decode cost on the Arc Pro B70).
Related, not duplicates: #628 / #637 (fused routed + shared-expert decode for FP8 per-tensor weights) and #623 (FP8 decode GEMV).
This PR covers int4 experts in the existing path and does not touch those.

checks the op against a dequantized fp32 reference and against on the same inputs: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B shapes (w13 1024x2048, w2 2048x512) and 5120x8192, 16 and 256 experts, 1-8 rows with one or two rows per expert, bf16 and fp16.
E2E (vLLM main + this branch, one B70): (palmfuture), single request, decode tok/s with , plus a short accuracy eval (gsm8k via lm_eval, 250 questions) for both.
Measured 2026-10-15 on one Arc Pro B70 (b70 tab, testq 004).

Kernel source = this branch ( and from fad147a) applied to release/0.1.15.4, which is the vllm-xpu-kernels in the vLLM nightly XPU image used (vllm 0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82); the op was built as an library fragment instead of a full rebuild.
Not run: a full build of upstream main 6b30c9b.
6 more cases (n=5120, k=8192, e=256) ran out of memory in the test itself: it built the random int4 weights as int64 (~40 GiB) before converting.

The test now generates them as uint8 and runs that shape with 16 experts only, like the existing cases for it (256 experts would still need ~10 GiB), so its 30 cases are exactly the shapes that passed above (the uint8 generation itself has not been run on a GPU yet).
: 40 passed (m=1 and m=4 without bias go through the new path).
E2E, vLLM nightly 3f1bcfd8 + this branch, palmfuture/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, , fp8 KV, 4K context, XPU graphs, no MTP, 1 request, 512-token answers, decode tok/s (code / prose):
gsm8k (first 100 test q, greedy, chat, no thinking)
With MTP (, 2K context) and the GEMV on: 157.3 / 118.7 tok/s, no GPU faults in the kernel log.
Not tested: other Intel GPUs (PVC, Xe3), expert parallelism.

Per layer at 1 token: gate_up 56 -> 18 us, down 34 -> 14 us.
Matches CUTLASS to 3e-4 relative error per call (stress test: 900 routings including outlier activations; 500 replays inside an XPU graph).
